continuation.text:
I changed the final check in `src/solution.py`. I did not run it or write any checks.

The function now returns `True` only if no resource is over capacity and at least one resource still has capacity left. Before, it returned `True` whenever no resource was over capacity. An allocation that uses up every resource completely now returns `False`.

I read "at least one resource must remain unallocated" as: at least one resource type has leftover capacity. The requirement could also mean every resource must keep some capacity free, which would be stricter. Tell me if you meant that.

An empty `resources` dict now returns `False`, because nothing can remain unallocated. That follows the new requirement, which takes precedence over the empty-input rule.

I left the validation, the immediate-failure cases and the signature as they were.
